newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed in dull, directionless market.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed in dull, directionless market.

text.p: Share prices were mixed, with the blue-chip Composite Index almost unchanged and volumes dominated by second board shares, as many investors waited for fresh trading factors, brokers and analysts said on Tuesday.
They said things had quietened down after the minor fund buying programs on Monday.
The Composite Index ended down 0.47 of a point at 1,076.93. The second board ended 3.98 points lower at 570.19
"The market was very dull, quiet and listless. The second board was more active compared with the main board," said Amarjit Chhina at BZW in Kuala Lumpur.
"I think there were various buy programs yesterday, spiced up things a bit. But today, we are back to where things really were," he said.
He said while people were concerned with the 2.1 billion ringgit trade deficit Malaysia reported for April, they were beginning to "treat it as it should be, a monthly figure".
A dealer with a Malaysian securities firm said motor stocks bucked the trend and ended stronger, but the reason was not clear.
"It could be on hopes that Proton and Hicom will announce better results on Friday," he said.
"It could also be because the yen is losing some of its recent strength," a dealer at a bank backed brokerage said. "This should boost auto firms' profits."
Proton was up 60 cents at 13.40 ringgit and Hicom rose six cents to 4.76 ringgit. Tan Chong gained two cents to 4.54, while DRB and Cycle & Carriage were unchanged at 6.0 ringgit and 17.20 ringgit.
Volume stood at 176.19 million shares against 243 million on Monday. Losers led gainers 365 to 211, with 166 shares unchanged.
Among blue-chip shares, Telekom was down 20 cents at 11.60 ringgit and Tenaga was up 10 cents at 11.50 ringgit.
Public Bank Bhd, which said it expected a 20 percent rise in its net profit this year, was up two cents at 3.58 ringgit.
Suria Capital, whose plan to start talks for a merger with MBf Capital was disallowed by Bank Negara, was down four cents at 2.66 ringgit.
Ekran, builder of the giant Bakun dam, whose heavily undersubscribed rights issue got listed today, ended the day 10 cents lower at 5.45 ringgit.
Most dealers said Ekran shares could have fallen further, but for support from some syndicates, market pressure groups.
They said the Ekran rights issue debacle had already been discounted by the market. On Monday, the share rose in the dying moments of the market to end 55 cents higher.
